common_name: Pearl Glam Beautyberry (Dark Purple Foliage Compact Beautyberry)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pearl Glam bears dark purple-black foliage year-round in addition to the classic vivid purple berry clusters.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; American beautyberry tolerates a wide range of conditions and needs little supplemental water once established. Pearl Glam bears striking dark purple-black foliage through the entire growing season, a departure from the plain green leaves of the straight species, paired in fall with the same eye-catching clusters of vivid purple berries that encircle the stems and persist after leaf drop, providing food for songbirds through winter. Its dark foliage color adds ornamental interest for months before the berry display even begins, and its more compact size fits smaller gardens than seedling-grown beautyberry. Prune hard in late winter to encourage vigorous new growth, since flowers and berries form on new wood.

common_name: Sparkleberry Winterberry Holly (Tall Heavy-Fruiting Hybrid Winterberry)

planting.note: Plant female shrubs alongside a compatible male pollinator such as Apollo or Jim Dandy in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade; Sparkleberry is a tall hybrid winterberry noted for exceptionally heavy, long-lasting berry set.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade, and site a compatible male pollinator such as Apollo within pollinating range, since winterberry is dioecious and female plants need a male nearby to set fruit. Sparkleberry, a hybrid between Ilex verticillata and the Japanese Ilex serrata, bears an exceptionally heavy crop of small, bright red berries that persist on bare branches well into winter, on a taller, more vigorous shrub than most straight-species winterberry cultivars. Its abundant, long-lasting fruit display is a favorite for winter arrangements and for feeding overwintering songbirds. Prune only lightly and only after flowering, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood.
sources: University of Connecticut Home & Garden Education Center

common_name: Winter Red Winterberry Holly (Heavy-Fruiting Compact Female Winterberry)

planting.note: Plant female shrubs alongside a compatible male pollinator such as Jim Dandy in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade; Winter Red is among the most widely planted and heaviest-fruiting winterberry cultivars available.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade, and site a compatible male pollinator such as Jim Dandy within pollinating range, since winterberry is dioecious and female plants need a male nearby to set fruit. Winter Red bears an exceptionally heavy, dense crop of bright red berries that coat the bare branches after leaf drop and persist well into winter, considered one of the most reliably prolific and widely available winterberry cultivars on the market. Its dependable, showy fruit display makes it a favorite for winter interest, holiday decorating, and feeding overwintering songbirds. Prune only lightly and only after flowering, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood.
sources: University of Connecticut Home & Garden Education Center

common_name: Berry Nice Winterberry Holly (Large-Fruited Female Winterberry)

planting.note: Plant female shrubs alongside a compatible male pollinator such as Jim Dandy in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade; Berry Nice bears unusually large, bright red berries on a vigorous, well-branched shrub.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade, and site a compatible male pollinator such as Jim Dandy within pollinating range, since winterberry is dioecious and female plants need a male nearby to set fruit. Berry Nice bears notably large, bright red berries in heavy clusters along the bare branches after leaf drop, standing out in size compared to many other winterberry cultivars, on a vigorous, well-branched shrub with good density. Its oversized, showy fruit provides strong winter interest and a reliable food source for overwintering songbirds. Prune only lightly and only after flowering, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood.
sources: University of Connecticut Home & Garden Education Center
